newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian shares gain, more seen.
newsitem.headline: Estonian shares gain, more seen.

text.p: Estonian shares gained for the second straight day on Friday and dealers said that a spell of profit-taking appeared to be over.

Dealers had predicted that this week's losses, which halted a record-smashing bull run, would be brief as the surge was supported by strong fundamentals, including solid results and raised profit forecasts.
Further gains are expected early next week, dealers said.
Total trade on the main list was 155 million kroons as the Talse index gained 3.60 percent to end the week at 418.06.
"There were buyers active in most shares during the day with interest in banking stocks the strongest," one trader said.
Hansapank was the most active stock with 76 million kroons traded to gain 2.50 kroons for a close of 219.50, six percent lower than last Friday's close.
Speculative interest in Uhispank pushed it to 105 kroons, a rise of 10.25 kroons with 24.7 million kroons traded.
On the free market, total trade was 5.4 million kroons with privatisation vouchers the most active.
Privatisation securities were down to 0.416 kroons from 0.44 with 3.6 million kroons traded.
